elements.text: An adage that has proven to be most veritable is the one pontificating that Time is a great healer, the truism however omitted by its ancient originator, was how rapidly time passes and dissipates. Although it was 64 years ago the memories are as clearly evident as if yesterday. A trio of neophytic Johannesburg orchidists (Freddie and Hettie Du Plooy and Doug McMurtry) drove to the Mother City to participate in a significant flower show where members of the then Orchid Society of South Africa had staged a landscape show stall of both indigenous and exotic orchids.

A trio of neophytic Johannesburg orchidists (Freddie and Hettie Du Plooy and Doug McMurtry) drove to the Mother City to participate in a significant flower show where members of the then Orchid Society of South Africa had staged a landscape show stall of both indigenous and exotic orchids.

elements.text: This noteworthy flower show in September, 1962 was held in the halls of the Goodwood Show Grounds, Cape Town displayed contributors from all sections of horticultural and floristic genre to acknowledge the celebration of the 50th Anniversary of the foundation of the National Botanic Garden, Kirstenbosch. During conversation at the show the Cape Town orchid members proffered sincere encouragement to the intrepid trio who were filled with enthusiasm. They returned home and immediately generated plans for the foundation for an orchid society, representing our Northerly Province (Johannesburg had an established Horticultural Society but no specialist Orchid Society)   Within a month of the Cape visit the Transvaal Orchid Society came into being; the three largest South African Provinces’ now had representative Orchid Societies - a major requisite for the formation of a National Orchid Council.

elements.text: The formation of the fledgling body to represent all orchid societies in South Africa at an International level faced a few minor difficulties but ‘time the healer’ has blurred those early disagreements. Perseverance paid off when all concerned successfully paved the way for the regulation and administration of standardised national Orchid Judging and the assurance that the publication of a quality Journal became a reality.  For a succinct history of the formation of the Council see SAOJ, 1970, March Vol 1, p.6.

During its now long development the rotating incumbents of the Board of Directors have supported the ideal that the SAOC should steadfastly and ethically maintain the highest standards in all aspects of orchidology, standards that would be recognised by reciprocity internationally. Success has been achieved; attested by our double issue journal Orchids South Africa in which international authors have made repeated contributions. South African orchidists have significantly enhanced the value of Orchid Wiz and finally our Judges have and shall continue to participate in World Orchid Conference’s and other International orchid judging events.

elements.text: Time has demonstrated that all the goals the SAOC set out to accomplish have come to fruition and as a senior foundation member my confidence is enhanced by the input of younger orchid enthusiasts who have taken on the responsibility. This positive knowledge leaves me satisfied and assured that they will ensure the permanence of the SAOC for succeeding generations.
